title: Planning the contract amendment
grammar: Futuro — going to (plano) × will (decisão na hora)
objective: Nesta aula você vai falar dos próximos passos de um aditivo contratual. 'We are going to issue a new proposal' é o plano que já existe; 'I will send it today' é a decisão que você toma na hora, na frente do cliente. Saber alternar as duas formas faz você soar organizado numa reunião de mudança de escopo.
intro: The client approved the change. Now everybody wants to know what happens next. We are going to update the drawings. We are going to issue a new proposal. The commercial team is going to prepare the amendment.

And then, in the middle of the meeting, someone asks for something. I will send you the document today. I will check that with the supplier. That is a decision you take at that moment, and English marks it with will.
vocab: The next step is going to be the technical review.
We are going to issue a new revision next week.
The deadline is going to move by two weeks.
There is going to be an additional cost of ten thousand reais.
I will update the drawing this afternoon.
We are going to review the schedule with the client.
practice: The ______ is going to be the technical review.
We are going to ______ a new revision next week.
The ______ is going to move by two weeks.
There is going to be an ______ of ten thousand reais.
I will ______ the drawing this afternoon.
We are going to review the ______ with the client.
What is the ______ after the approval?

audio.title: What happens next
audio.text: Thank you for the approval. Let me explain what happens next. We are going to update the layout drawings this week. Then we are going to issue revision C and send it for your comments. The commercial team is going to prepare the contract amendment, and I think it is going to be ready by Friday. The deadline for the mechanical package is going to move by two weeks, but the final date is not going to change. Do you need the cost breakdown today? Yes? No problem, I will send it to you this afternoon. And I will call the supplier to confirm the new delivery date.

readAloud: We are going to update the drawings this week.
The commercial team is going to prepare the amendment.
The deadline is going to move by two weeks.
I will send it to you this afternoon.
I will call the supplier to confirm the date.
fill: We ___ update the drawings this week. (be going to)
The team ___ prepare the amendment. (be going to)
The deadline ___ move by two weeks. (be going to)
No problem, I ___ it to you this afternoon. (will send)
I ___ the supplier to confirm the date. (will call)
There ___ be an additional cost. (be going to)
The final date ___ change. (be not going to)
Don't worry, I ___ you tomorrow. (will inform)
qa: What are you going to do next?
We are going to update the drawings and issue revision C.
Who is going to prepare the amendment?
The commercial team is going to prepare it.
Is the final date going to change?
No, it is not going to change.
Can you send me the cost breakdown?
Yes, I will send it to you this afternoon.
Who is going to talk to the supplier?
I will call him today.
sentences: We are going to update the drawings this week.
The commercial team is going to prepare the amendment.
The deadline is going to move by two weeks.
The final date is not going to change.
I will send it to you this afternoon.
I will call the supplier to confirm the date.
What are you going to do next?
There is going to be an additional cost.
grammarPoint:
be going to = plano que já existe antes da conversa.
We are going to update the drawings this week.
Forma: am / is / are + going to + verbo.

will = decisão tomada agora, na hora de falar. Também para promessa e oferta.
No problem, I will send it this afternoon.
Forma: will + verbo (igual para todas as pessoas).

Negativa: is not going to change · won't change.
deepDive:
O teste simples: se você pode dizer "já estava combinado", use going to. Se você acabou de decidir enquanto falava, use will.

going to também serve para previsão com evidência: Look at the schedule — the deadline is going to move. Você está olhando o dado.

will aparece depois de opinião: I think it will be ready by Friday. · I'm sure the client will approve it. Depois de I think, I hope, probably, o normal é will.

Contrações da fala: I'll, we'll, he'll, it'll · negativa: won't.

Depois de when e if, não use will: I'll call you when the drawing is ready. (não: when the drawing will be ready)
examples: We are going to update the drawings this week.
Vamos atualizar os desenhos esta semana.
The team is going to prepare the amendment.
A equipe vai preparar o aditivo.
The deadline is going to move by two weeks.
O prazo vai mudar em duas semanas.
The final date is not going to change.
A data final não vai mudar.
I will send it to you this afternoon.
Eu envio para você esta tarde.
I think it will be ready by Friday.
Acho que estará pronto até sexta.
I'll call you when the drawing is ready.
Eu te ligo quando o desenho estiver pronto.
There is going to be an additional cost.
Vai haver um custo adicional.
mistakes: We are going update the drawings.
We are going to update the drawings.
Falta o to: going to + verbo.
I will to send it this afternoon.
I will send it this afternoon.
Depois de will o verbo vem sem to.
The team are going to prepare it.
The team is going to prepare it.
team é singular em inglês americano: is.
I'll call you when the drawing will be ready.
I'll call you when the drawing is ready.
Depois de when não se usa will.
We will update the drawings, it is already in the plan.
We are going to update the drawings.
Plano já existente pede going to.
quick: We ___ update the drawings. (be going to)
The team ___ prepare the amendment. (be going to)
No problem, I ___ it today. (will send)
The final date ___ change. (be not going to)
I'll call you when the drawing ___ ready. (be)

celebrate.en: Great. You can now close a meeting with a clear list of next steps — and everybody knows who does what.
celebrate.pt: Ótimo. Agora você fecha uma reunião com uma lista clara de próximos passos — e todo mundo sabe quem faz o quê.

title: Asking a supplier for a quotation
grammar: Pedidos educados — Could you / Would you / I would like
objective: Nesta aula você vai escrever e falar com fornecedores estrangeiros sem soar rude. Em inglês, 'Send me the quotation' é uma ordem; 'Could you send me the quotation?' é um pedido normal de trabalho. Você vai treinar Could you, Would you, I would like to e Would it be possible to — as quatro fórmulas que aparecem em toda cotação internacional.
intro: When you write to a supplier in Germany, Italy or China, your English is the only thing they see. A direct sentence that sounds normal in Portuguese can sound impolite in English, and that changes the answer you get.
The fix is easy and mechanical. Could you send us your quotation? I would like to receive the technical documents. Would it be possible to reduce the delivery time? Same message, much better result.
vocab: Could you send us your quotation by Friday?
I would like to send you a request for quotation.
Would it be possible to have a technical clarification call?
Could you confirm the scope limit of your supply?
I would like to receive the datasheet of the fan.
The supplier is going to answer us next week.
practice: Could you send us your ______ by Friday?
I would like to send you a ______.
Would it be possible to have a ______ call?
Could you confirm the ______ of your supply?
I would like to receive the ______ of the fan.
The ______ is going to answer us next week.
Please send the ______ in PDF and in Excel.
The ______ is not clear in your proposal.

audio.title: A call with a foreign supplier
audio.text: Good afternoon. Thank you for joining the call. I would like to talk about the request for quotation we sent last week. First, could you confirm that you received all the documents? Good. Second, would it be possible to send us the datasheet of the fan before the quotation? We need it for the layout. Third, could you clarify the scope limit of your supply? We are not sure about the motor and the base frame. And one last question. Would you be able to indicate the delivery time in weeks, not in months? That would help us a lot. Thank you very much.

readAloud: Could you send us your quotation by Friday?
I would like to receive the datasheet.
Would it be possible to reduce the delivery time?
Could you clarify the scope limit of your supply?
Thank you very much for your help.
fill: I ___ to receive the datasheet. (would like)
___ it be possible to reduce the delivery time? (would)
___ you be able to send it today? (would)
I would like ___ the technical documents. (receive)
Would it be possible ___ a call tomorrow? (have)
Could you ___ me the price in euros? (give)
qa: Could you send us your quotation?
Yes, of course. I will send it by Friday.
Would it be possible to have a clarification call?
Yes, certainly. Would Tuesday be convenient?
Could you confirm the scope limit?
Yes. The motor is included, but the base frame is not.
What would you like to receive first?
I would like to receive the datasheet of the fan.
Would you be able to reduce the delivery time?
I'm afraid that would be difficult, but I will check.
sentences: Could you send us your quotation by Friday?
I would like to receive the datasheet of the fan.
Would it be possible to reduce the delivery time?
Could you clarify the scope limit of your supply?
Would you be able to send it today?
Thank you very much for your help.
I would like to talk about the request for quotation.
Would Tuesday be convenient for a call?
grammarPoint:
As quatro fórmulas do pedido educado:

1. Could you + verbo? — Could you send us your quotation?
2. Would you be able to + verbo? — Would you be able to confirm the price?
3. I would like to + verbo — I would like to receive the datasheet.
4. Would it be possible to + verbo? — Would it be possible to reduce the lead time?

Regra fixa: depois de could e would o verbo vem na forma base, sem to e sem -s.
Mas depois de would like e possible, entra to + verbo.
deepDive:
A escala da educação, do mais direto ao mais formal:
Send me the quotation. (ordem — só para instrução interna)
Please send me the quotation. (aceitável por e-mail)
Could you send me the quotation? (padrão de trabalho)
Would it be possible to send me the quotation? (formal, primeiro contato)

I want × I would like: I want the datasheet soa infantil e exigente. Use sempre I would like (ou a contração I'd like).

Como responder a um pedido:
sim → Of course. · Certainly. · Sure, no problem.
não → I'm afraid that won't be possible. · That would be difficult, but I'll check.

Fecho de e-mail para fornecedor: Thank you in advance. · Looking forward to your reply. · Best regards,
examples: Could you send us your quotation by Friday?
Você poderia nos enviar sua cotação até sexta?
I would like to receive the datasheet.
Eu gostaria de receber a folha de dados.
Would it be possible to reduce the delivery time?
Seria possível reduzir o prazo de entrega?
Would you be able to confirm the price today?
Você conseguiria confirmar o preço hoje?
Could you clarify the scope limit?
Você poderia esclarecer o limite de escopo?
I'm afraid that won't be possible.
Infelizmente isso não será possível.
Of course. I will send it this afternoon.
Claro. Envio esta tarde.
Thank you in advance. Best regards.
Desde já, obrigado. Atenciosamente.
mistakes: Could you to send us the quotation?
Could you send us the quotation?
Depois de could não entra to.
Could you sends me the datasheet?
Could you send me the datasheet?
Depois de could o verbo fica sem -s.
I would like receive the datasheet.
I would like to receive the datasheet.
would like pede to + verbo.
I want the quotation until Friday.
I would like the quotation by Friday.
Use would like, e prazo é by, não until.
Would be possible to have a call?
Would it be possible to have a call?
Falta o sujeito it.
quick: Would ___ be possible to have a call?
___ you be able to confirm today?

celebrate.en: Very good. Your emails to foreign suppliers now sound professional — and professional emails get faster answers.
celebrate.pt: Muito bom. Seus e-mails para fornecedores estrangeiros agora soam profissionais — e e-mail profissional recebe resposta mais rápido.

title: Delivery, warranty and documents
grammar: Preposições de tempo — in / on / at / by / until / for
objective: Nesta aula você vai falar de prazos sem margem para dúvida. 'By Friday' significa até sexta, e 'until Friday' significa durante todo o período até sexta — a diferença entre as duas já causou muita confusão com fornecedor. Você também vai fixar in (mês, ano), on (dia, data) e at (hora), além de for e since.
intro: Delivery time, warranty period, document submission. Three topics, and all three depend on one small word that everybody underestimates: the preposition.

The fan will be delivered in September. The test is on 14 June. The call is at three o'clock. Please send the drawings by Friday. The warranty is valid for twenty-four months. Get these right and nobody has to ask again.
vocab: The delivery time is twenty weeks from the order.
The warranty is valid for twenty-four months.
Please send the technical documents by Friday.
The submission is due on the fifteenth.
We placed the order in March.
The lead time did not change since last year.
practice: The ______ is twenty weeks from the order.
The ______ is valid for twenty-four months.
The ______ is due on the fifteenth.
The ______ did not change since last year.
The ______ starts on the date of delivery.
We need the ______ before the design review.

audio.title: Confirming dates with the supplier
audio.text: Let me confirm all the dates with you. We placed the order in March, on the tenth of March. The delivery time is twenty weeks, so the equipment arrives in August. The technical documents must be sent by the thirtieth of April. That means before the thirtieth, not on the thirtieth. The design review is on the fifth of May, at ten o'clock in the morning. The warranty is valid for twenty four months from delivery, or for eighteen months from start up, whichever comes first. And please remember, the drawings stay under review until the client approves them.

readAloud: We placed the order in March.
The design review is on the fifth of May.
The call is at ten o'clock.
Please send the documents by Friday.
The warranty is valid for twenty-four months.
fill: The design review is ___ the fifth of May. (in/on/at)
The drawings stay under review ___ the client approves them. (by/until)
The warranty is valid ___ twenty-four months. (for/since)
The lead time has not changed ___ last year. (for/since)
qa: When did you place the order?
We placed it in March, on the tenth.
When is the design review?
It is on the fifth of May, at ten o'clock.
When do you need the documents?
We need them by Friday, so before Friday.
How long is the warranty valid?
It is valid for twenty-four months from delivery.
How long have the drawings been under review?
They have been under review since last week.
sentences: We placed the order in March.
The design review is on the fifth of May.
The call is at ten o'clock.
Please send the documents by Friday.
The drawings stay under review until the client approves them.
The warranty is valid for twenty-four months.
The lead time has not changed since last year.
The equipment arrives in August.
grammarPoint:
in / on / at — do maior para o menor:
in + mês, ano, estação, parte do dia → in March · in 2026 · in the morning
on + dia da semana e data → on Friday · on the fifth of May
at + hora → at ten o'clock · at noon

by × until — o par que mais causa problema:
by = até (no máximo), prazo final → Send it by Friday. (pode ser antes)
until = até (durante todo o tempo) → They stay under review until Friday.

for = duração (for 24 months) · since = ponto de início (since last year)
deepDive:
Por que by × until vale dinheiro: Please deliver by 30 April significa que o dia 29 está ótimo. Please deliver until 30 April não faz sentido para uma entrega — e o fornecedor vai perguntar de novo, perdendo uma semana.

Exceções que você precisa saber:
at the weekend (britânico) / on the weekend (americano)
at night, mas in the morning / afternoon / evening
on Monday morning (quando vem o dia, o on ganha)

Sem preposição nenhuma antes de: next week, last month, this year, every Friday, tomorrow, yesterday.
✗ in next week → ✓ next week

Outras que aparecem em prazo: from March to May · within 30 days (dentro de) · during the shutdown · after delivery.
examples: We placed the order in March.
Fizemos o pedido em março.
The design review is on the fifth of May.
A revisão de projeto é no dia cinco de maio.
The call is at ten o'clock.
A ligação é às dez horas.
Please send the documents by Friday.
Por favor, envie os documentos até sexta (no máximo).
They stay under review until Friday.
Eles ficam em análise até sexta (o tempo todo).
The warranty is valid for twenty-four months.
A garantia vale por vinte e quatro meses.
The lead time has not changed since last year.
O prazo de fabricação não mudou desde o ano passado.
We must answer within thirty days.
Precisamos responder dentro de trinta dias.
mistakes: The review is in the fifth of May.
The review is on the fifth of May.
Data leva on.
Please send it until Friday.
Please send it by Friday.
Prazo final é by; until é duração.
The warranty is valid since twenty-four months.
The warranty is valid for twenty-four months.
Duração pede for.
We will meet in next week.
We will meet next week.
next week não leva preposição.
The call is in ten o'clock.
The call is at ten o'clock.
Hora leva at.
quick: The review is ___ the fifth of May.

celebrate.en: Excellent. Deadlines and warranties are now unambiguous in your English — and that saves emails, calls and money.
celebrate.pt: Excelente. Prazos e garantias agora ficam sem ambiguidade no seu inglês — e isso economiza e-mail, ligação e dinheiro.

title: At an international congress
grammar: Comparativos e superlativos (bigger / more efficient / the best)
objective: Nesta aula você vai comparar tecnologias e softwares, que é exatamente o que se faz num congresso técnico. Você vai aprender as duas regras: adjetivo curto ganha -er e the -est (faster, the fastest); adjetivo longo usa more e the most (more efficient, the most efficient). E vai fixar a estrutura completa com than e as ... as.
intro: A congress is three days of comparisons. This scrubber is more efficient than the old one. This software is faster than the version we use. That solution is the most expensive on the market.
To talk about what you saw, you need comparatives and superlatives. The rule depends only on the length of the adjective, and once you see it, you never forget it.
vocab: This technology is newer than the one we use.
The new filter is more efficient than the old one.
The emission level is lower than the legal limit.
This software is easier to use than AutoCAD.
They are the biggest supplier in Europe.
That was the most interesting solution at the congress.
practice: This ______ is newer than the one we use.
The new filter is more ______ than the old one.
The ______ level is lower than the legal limit.
This ______ is easier to use than AutoCAD.
They are the biggest ______ in Europe.
That was the most interesting ______ at the congress.
The best ______ was in the German stand.
A more ______ fan uses less energy.

audio.title: Report from the congress
audio.text: I went to the congress in Milan last week and I want to share three points. First, the new ceramic filters are more efficient than our bag filters, but they are also much more expensive. Second, the emission limits in Europe are lower than in Brazil, so the equipment is bigger and the control is stricter. Third, and this was the most interesting part for me, there is new software for three D piping design. It is faster than the software we use today and it is easier to learn. It is not as complete as our current system, but it is improving very quickly.

readAloud: The new filter is more efficient than the old one.
This software is faster than the one we use.
That was the most interesting solution at the congress.
They are the biggest supplier in Europe.
It is not as complete as our current system.
fill: The new filter is ___ than the old one. (efficient)
This software is ___ than the one we use. (fast)
That was ___ solution at the congress. (interesting)
The emission level is ___ than the legal limit. (low)
It is not ___ complete ___ our current system. (as ... as)
That was ___ presentation of the day. (good)
qa: How was the congress?
It was very good. The most interesting part was the new software.
Is the ceramic filter better than the bag filter?
It is more efficient, but it is also much more expensive.
Is the new software fast?
Yes, it is faster than the software we use today.
Who is the biggest supplier in Europe?
The German company is the biggest one.
Are the emission limits the same as in Brazil?
No, they are lower than in Brazil.
sentences: The new filter is more efficient than the old one.
This software is faster than the one we use.
That was the most interesting solution at the congress.
They are the biggest supplier in Europe.
The emission limits are lower than in Brazil.
It is not as complete as our current system.
This one is much more expensive.
That was the best presentation of the day.
grammarPoint:
Adjetivo curto (1 sílaba, ou 2 terminando em -y):
comparativo + er · superlativo the + est
fast → faster → the fastest · easy → easier → the easiest

Adjetivo longo (2 sílabas ou mais):
comparativo more + · superlativo the most +
efficient → more efficient → the most efficient

A palavra da comparação é than: faster than the old one.
Para igualdade: as complete as our system.
deepDive:
Irregulares — só três, e são os mais usados:
good → better → the best
bad → worse → the worst
far → further → the furthest

Ortografia: consoante + vogal + consoante dobra a letra: big → bigger · hot → hotter. Terminado em -y vira -ier: easy → easier.

Para reforçar a comparação: much more expensive · far better · a lot faster.
Para reduzir: slightly more efficient · a little bigger.

Superlativo pede o artigo the e costuma vir com in ou of: the biggest supplier in Europe · the best presentation of the day.

Negativa de igualdade: It is not as complete as our system. = It is less complete than our system.
examples: The new filter is more efficient than the old one.
O novo filtro é mais eficiente que o antigo.
This software is faster than the one we use.
Este software é mais rápido que o que usamos.
That was the most interesting solution.
Aquela foi a solução mais interessante.
They are the biggest supplier in Europe.
Eles são o maior fornecedor da Europa.
The emission limits are lower than in Brazil.
Os limites de emissão são mais baixos que no Brasil.
It is not as complete as our current system.
Não é tão completo quanto o nosso sistema atual.
This one is much more expensive.
Este aqui é bem mais caro.
That was the best presentation of the day.
Aquela foi a melhor apresentação do dia.
mistakes: The new filter is more efficienter.
The new filter is more efficient.
Não use more e -er juntos.
This software is faster that the old one.
This software is faster than the old one.
A comparação usa than, não that.
It was the most best presentation.
It was the best presentation.
best já é superlativo.
They are biggest supplier in Europe.
They are the biggest supplier in Europe.
Superlativo pede o artigo the.
It is not so complete than our system.
It is not as complete as our system.
A estrutura de igualdade é as ... as.
quick: The new filter is ___ than the old one. (efficient)
That was ___ presentation of the day. (good)

celebrate.en: Very good. You can now come back from a congress and explain, in English, exactly what is better and why.
celebrate.pt: Muito bom. Agora você volta de um congresso e explica, em inglês, exatamente o que é melhor e por quê.

title: Presenting the Delta Ducon equipment line
grammar: can / can't para capacidade + descrever equipamento (adjetivo antes do substantivo)
objective: Nesta aula você vai apresentar a linha de equipamentos da Delta Ducon em inglês. Você vai usar can e can't para falar do que cada equipamento consegue fazer ('The baghouse can handle 200 thousand cubic metres per hour', 'It can't work above 250 degrees') e vai aprender a ordem correta dos adjetivos na descrição técnica, que em inglês é o contrário do português.
intro: Delta Ducon has a full line of air and water pollution control equipment: baghouses, electrostatic precipitators, scrubbers, cyclones and fans. In front of a client, you have to say what each one does, what it can handle and where it should not be used.
Can and can't are the verbs of capability. And remember one small but very visible rule: in English the adjective comes before the noun. A high temperature filter, not a filter of high temperature.
vocab: The baghouse can handle a very high dust load.
An electrostatic precipitator can treat large gas volumes.
A wet scrubber can remove gases as well as dust.
A cyclone can't reach very low emission levels.
This unit can treat a gas volume of 200,000 cubic metres per hour.
The maximum operating temperature is 250 degrees.
practice: The ______ can handle a very high dust load.
An ______ can treat large gas volumes.
A wet ______ can remove gases as well as dust.
A ______ can't reach very low emission levels.
This unit can treat a ______ of 200,000 cubic metres per hour.
A ______ is the simplest equipment in the line.
The ______ uses filter bags to capture the dust.

audio.title: Presenting the equipment line
audio.text: Let me present our equipment line. We have four main products. The cyclone is the simplest one. It is cheap and strong, but it can't reach low emission levels, so we use it as a pre cleaner. The baghouse uses filter bags. It can reach very low emissions, and it can handle a high dust load, but it can't work with wet gas. The electrostatic precipitator can treat very large gas volumes with a low pressure drop. It is expensive, but it works very well in big plants. Finally, the wet scrubber can remove gases as well as dust, and it can work at high temperature.

readAloud: The baghouse can reach very low emissions.
It can't work with wet gas.
An electrostatic precipitator can treat large gas volumes.
A cyclone can't reach low emission levels.
A wet scrubber can work at high temperature.
fill: The baghouse ___ reach very low emissions. (can)
It ___ work with wet gas. (can not)
An EP ___ treat very large gas volumes. (can)
A cyclone ___ reach low emission levels. (can not)
The unit ___ handle 200,000 cubic metres per hour. (can)
qa: What can the baghouse do?
It can reach very low emissions and handle a high dust load.
Can it work with wet gas?
No, it can't. For wet gas we use a scrubber.
Which equipment can treat the largest gas volume?
The electrostatic precipitator can.
Can a cyclone reach low emission levels?
No, it can't. We use it as a pre-cleaner.
What is the maximum operating temperature?
It is 250 degrees for the standard baghouse.
sentences: The baghouse can reach very low emissions.
It can't work with wet gas.
An electrostatic precipitator can treat large gas volumes.
A cyclone can't reach low emission levels.
A wet scrubber can work at high temperature.
This unit can handle 200,000 cubic metres per hour.
The maximum operating temperature is 250 degrees.
We use the cyclone as a pre-cleaner.
grammarPoint:
can / can't = o que o equipamento consegue ou não consegue fazer.

Afirmativa: The baghouse can reach very low emissions.
Negativa: It can't work with wet gas.
Pergunta: Can the scrubber work at 250 degrees?

Regras fixas: depois de can o verbo fica na forma base — sem to e sem -s. E can é igual para todas as pessoas.

Adjetivo antes do substantivo: a high temperature filter, a wet scrubber, a large gas volume.
deepDive:
Descrição técnica em inglês é montada de trás para frente. Em português: filtro de mangas para alta temperatura. Em inglês, o substantivo principal vai por último: a high temperature bag filter.

A ordem usual dos adjetivos: opinião → tamanho → idade → forma → cor → origem → material → finalidade + substantivo.
a large new German bag filter

Primos do can:
be able to — mesmo sentido, e serve para outros tempos: It will be able to treat 200,000 m³/h.
could — capacidade no passado: The old unit could only treat half of that.

Números técnicos na fala: 200,000 m³/h = two hundred thousand cubic metres per hour · 250 °C = two hundred and fifty degrees Celsius · 0.5% = zero point five per cent.
examples: The baghouse can reach very low emissions.
O filtro de mangas consegue atingir emissões muito baixas.
It can't work with wet gas.
Ele não consegue operar com gás úmido.
An electrostatic precipitator can treat large gas volumes.
Um precipitador eletrostático consegue tratar grandes vazões de gás.
Can the scrubber work at 250 degrees?
O lavador consegue operar a 250 graus?
This is a high temperature bag filter.
Este é um filtro de mangas para alta temperatura.
The old unit could only treat half of that.
A unidade antiga só conseguia tratar a metade disso.
It will be able to treat 200,000 cubic metres per hour.
Ele conseguirá tratar 200 mil metros cúbicos por hora.
We use the cyclone as a pre-cleaner.
Usamos o ciclone como pré-coletor.
mistakes: The baghouse can to reach low emissions.
The baghouse can reach low emissions.
Depois de can não entra to.
It can works with wet gas.
It can work with wet gas.
Depois de can o verbo fica sem -s.
This is a filter of high temperature.
This is a high temperature filter.
Em inglês o adjetivo vem antes do substantivo.
Can the scrubber works at 250 degrees?
Can the scrubber work at 250 degrees?
Na pergunta com can o verbo fica na forma base.
It doesn't can work with wet gas.
It can't work with wet gas.
can já forma a negativa sozinho: can't.
quick: It ___ work with wet gas. (can not)
The old unit ___ only treat half of that. (could)
